digest.component_or_area: enrichment queue and ticket digest history storage
propositions: Physical deletion of committed UUID events provides no repository size benefit because blobs persist in git history indefinitely, making retention-via-prune a cost-without-benefit strategy that breaks cross-clone merges

The dominant read cost in queue reduction is file opens (4977 opens per full-store scan, 0.372s wall), not filesystem dirents, and grows unbounded with event accumulation while digest sidecar already reads newest-first at O(1)

A merge-safe removal must rename to a deterministic source-derived path with identical content; removal paired with fresh-UUID adds violates this rule and causes rename/rename conflicts under git merge

Bounding the read via newest-first suffix scan—using monotonic timestamp prefixes in filenames to stop iteration early—achieves the performance goal without deleting, renaming, or modifying any committed event
The design reduces file opens from 4977 to 1658 per full-store scan (67% reduction) while preserving invariant I1 and requiring no retention lifecycle or merge-semantics change
